title: WEF Data Equity 2024 roster continuity depth 4
summary: The 2024 Advancing Data Equity contributor roster shows strong continuity with the 2023 council:18 of 19 2023 council members recur, Katherine Hsiao remains listed at Palantir, two members are added, and one 2023 member is absent. Several professional-role changes can now be modeled temporally rather than backfilled.

sources.title: Advancing Data Equity:An Action-Oriented Framework PDF
WEF Advancing Data Equity 2024 mirrored full text

gaps: The official www3.weforum.org 2024 PDF endpoint timed out during this pass; contributor text was recovered from an indexed mirror while official WEF HTML independently verifies the report title, date and that it was produced by members of the Global Future Council on Data Equity.
caveats: A contributor-roster listing establishes named council participation in the report's contributor section, not section-level authorship or employer institutional endorsement.
Absence from one contributor roster is not evidence of no other WEF participation in the same year.

provenance.method: official WEF publication verification plus temporal comparison of recovered 2023 and 2024 contributor rosters

data.question: How did the Global Future Council on Data Equity roster and affiliations change between the 2023 and 2024 outputs?
data.method: Compare the 2023 WEF-branded report contributor page to the 2024 Advancing Data Equity contributor section recovered from an indexed copy; use official WEF publication metadata and person profiles to anchor report identity and current role context.
data.scope: Named council members and WEF council managers appearing in the 2024 report contributor section.
findings: The official WEF page dates Advancing Data Equity:An Action-Oriented Framework to 11 September 2024 and states that it was produced by members of the Global Future Council on Data Equity.
The 2024 contributor roster contains 20 council members. Eighteen of the 19 council members named in the 2023 report recur in 2024.
Katherine Hsiao recurs in the 2024 council-member list with the same published role:Executive Vice-President and Head of Health and Life Sciences, Palantir Technologies.
Arathi Sethumadhavan, listed in the 2023 roster as User Research Scientist, Technology and Society, Google, is not present in the recovered 2024 council-member roster.

Kathy Baxter, listed as Principal Architect, Responsible Artificial Intelligence and Technology, Salesforce, and Georges-Simon Ulrich, listed as Director General, Swiss Federal Statistical Office, appear in the 2024 roster but not the 2023 roster.

Alberto Giovanni Busetto changes from Group Senior Vice-President and Head of Data and Artificial Intelligence, Adecco Group in the 2023 report to Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer, HealthAI in the 2024 report.

Arti Garg remains at Hewlett Packard Enterprise but the listed role changes from AI Chief Strategist in 2023 to Head of Technology Strategy and Evaluation and Senior Distinguished Technologist in 2024.
Jacqueline Lu remains tied to Helpful Places; the 2024 contributor section renders the organization as Helpful Places (DTPR).
The recovered 2024 contributor section separately lists World Economic Forum council managers Karla Yee Amezaga and Stephanie Teeuwen; these should not be conflated with the 20 council members.
conclusions: The 2024 output demonstrates year-over-year continuity of Hsiao's named Palantir-affiliated council participation across two successive Data Equity publications.
The council network is stable but not static:the report pair supports explicit temporal membership and employment-role transitions rather than a single timeless affiliation graph.
limitations: The 2024 full contributor text is currently backed by an indexed artifact mirror because the official WEF PDF host timed out; the official WEF publication page independently verifies the report and council provenance.
unresolved: Whether any individual council member had section-level drafting responsibility beyond being named in the contributor roster.
Whether Palantir as an institution had any role beyond Hsiao's employer affiliation; no such institutional role is established by the reviewed sources.
